title: LOOKING AT THE LAND WITH THE WRONG EYES

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Reubenites and Gadites, who had very large herds and flocks, saw that the lands of Jazer and Gilead were suitable for livestock. So they came to Moses and Eleazar the priest and to the leaders of the community, and said, "Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo and Beon—the land the Lord subdued before the people of Israel—are suitable for livestock, and your servants have livestock." - Num 32:1-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The tribes of Reuben and Gad had done well for themselves. Their herds and flocks were large, and when they saw the rich grazing land east of the Jordan, they immediately thought, "This suits us." On the surface there was nothing wrong with noticing good pasture. But underneath, a question was forming in their hearts: would they settle for what looked good to them, even if it meant stopping short of where God was leading the whole nation?

This is a temptation we all know. God has promised something ahead, but along the way we spot something comfortable, convenient, and immediately useful. The land east of the Jordan was good — but it was not the Promised Land. It is possible to settle for good things and miss God's best, simply because the good thing is right in front of us and requires no further faith.

Notice how they saw the land through the lens of their possessions: "we have livestock, and this suits our livestock." Our stuff can quietly start steering our decisions. When our possessions shape our choices more than God's purposes do, we are in danger.

Jesus warned us not to store up treasures on earth but to seek first His kingdom (Matt 6:33). The good land is not always the right land. Before we settle anywhere, it is worth asking: am I choosing this because it suits me, or because it fits where God is leading me?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you tempted to settle for a "good" thing that stops short of God's best?
2. How much do your possessions influence your major decisions?
3. What would it look like to seek God's kingdom first in a current choice?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from settling for what merely suits me when You are leading me to something better. Help me to seek Your kingdom first in every decision. Amen.
